# p24 journal — 32 y/o man, 177 cm, 88 kg, upgrading from old BodyTracker (2 months of data)

## Day 1 (Sun 2026-10-04) — the update
- Opened the app: big "What's new in BodyTracker" popup. Long list (smarter maintenance with a ± range, many meals per day, "Day complete", water-weight tags, body fat, safer targets, backups, dates fixed, "your maintenance number may change"). Had to scroll a lot to reach the buttons at the bottom ("Make a backup", "Next: confirm your profile"). Readable, not scary. It says "Everything you logged is still here", which is what I wanted to hear.
- **Popup test:** tapped the dark area outside the popup before touching any buttons -> nothing happened, popup stayed open. Good; I couldn't accidentally skip it. (screens/1790454604966.png)
- Tapped "Make a backup" inside the popup. It didn't download straight away — it closed the What's-new popup and opened a "Your data" panel instead, where I had to tap "Full backup (JSON)". Slightly unexpected (I thought the button *was* the backup) but fine. File landed: downloads/bodytracker-backup-2026-10-04.json. "Last backup: 2026-10-04" updated.
- When I closed "Your data" with ✕, the profile step still appeared ("Set up your profile") — good, the flow wasn't lost by detouring into backups.
- **Migration check:** "Your data" panel showed Weigh-ins 45, Food entries 49, Complete days 49, range 2026-08-05 → 2026-10-03. Body tab "Recent entries" lists all my old weights (86.5 on 10-03, 87.2 on 10-02 …). Food log date picker on 2026-08-05 shows my old single 2237 kcal entry with macros. Everything seems to be there. All 49 old food days were automatically marked "Day complete" (☑) — makes sense since back then I always entered one full-day total, but the app never asked me.
- **Profile step:** yellow box said: "Earlier versions filled in height 175 cm, age 25 and activity 1.45 automatically if you never changed them — please check these values." Exactly my case, I never set them. Fields showed 175 / 25 / 86.5 kg (my last old weigh-in), Male formula, Lightly active (× 1.375) pre-picked. Small thing: the note says the old activity was 1.45 but the choices are 1.375 or 1.55, and it silently picked 1.375.
- Changed to 177 cm, 32 y, weight 88.1 (this morning's scale), kept Lightly active, answered "Yes" to eating the same for 2+ weeks, weekly update day Sun. Saved. The weight change added a 88.1 kg weigh-in for today (note under the form warned about that). "Explain the math" confirms it now uses 177 cm and age 32.
- After saving: iPhone "Add to Home Screen" hint (Got it). Nutrition tab: maintenance 2,720 ± 280 "Measured, 78% from your data", target 2,200 kcal/day, lose 0.6%/wk, "On track". Goal 80 kg (from old version) — 15 weeks away.
- Logged 4 meals at real times. Pizza had no macros -> day total then only shows kcal, drops the protein/carb totals for the day entirely (a bit annoying; would like to see "95 g protein + unknown").
- "Explain the math" is pure formulas (Hall 2008, Forbes, MAD…). Way over my head, closed it.
- Ate 2,111 today, under 2,200. Marked day complete.

## Day 2 (Mon)
- Tapped the big weight number ("Weight") expecting to add a weigh-in; it opened the Weight trend chart instead. The add button is the "+ Weight" one. Minor learning curve.
- "+ Weight" form: date/time prefilled, weight, body fat, fat mass, muscle mass. Entered 87.6. Goal progress went 27% -> 32% toward 80 kg.
- 4 meals, 2,198 kcal — right on the 2,200 target. Marked complete.

## Day 3 (Tue)
- 86.6 kg, goal bar 41%. Trend weight 87.3.
- Breakfast (foul & bread, numbers from my usual app) got a warning "Macros add up to ~716 kcal (18% from the logged calories). One of the numbers may be off." Fair, the numbers I copy are rough. Left it.
- Big lunch (fish & rice 1,089, no macros). 2,782 total — well over 2,200. The app doesn't show "remaining for today" anywhere I can see in the food log, just the day total, so I only noticed afterwards.

## Day 4 (Wed)
- 87.3 kg (up from 86.6 — goal bar went back from 41% to 34%, a bit discouraging; the % bar uses the raw daily weight, not the trend).
- 2,123 kcal. The "macros add up to ~X kcal (21% off)" warning showed on every meal today. My numbers are what the labels say; I can't do much about it. Starting to ignore it.

## Day 5 (Thu)
- 86.7 kg. Burger day, 2,490 kcal — over again. Nutrition summary: avg intake 2,341, "5 of last 7 days complete" (the two gap days from the old app before the update). Protein 146 g vs 157 g target "average of 3 complete days with protein logged" — so days where one meal had no macros don't count for protein. Makes sense once I read it.
- Maintenance/target numbers haven't moved since Sunday — the screen says they update weekly on Sunday, so that's expected.

## Day 6 (Fri)
- 87.4 kg. 2,526 kcal. When I tapped the Body tab, it opened scrolled halfway down (on the tape measurements) instead of at the top — it remembers where I was, which made me think my weigh-in hadn't saved until I scrolled up. It had.

## Day 7 (Sat)
- 88.5 kg — highest this week, goal bar dropped to 23%. Annoying, but the trend line says 87.4 so I'm treating it as water (big pasta / fish-rice days).
- Profile check via ⚙ -> "Edit profile": still 177 cm / 32 y / Male / Lightly active, weight field shows latest 88.5. Profile saved correctly. Pressing Escape did not close the profile window (✕ did).

## Week 1 (review on Sat 2026-10-10)
- App says: maintenance **2,720 ± 280 kcal/day**, label **Measured** (78% from my data), target **2,200 kcal/day** (lose 0.6%/wk = −0.52 kg/wk), recommendation "**On track.** Your estimated rate (−0.65 to −0.06 kg/week) includes your target of −0.52 kg/week. Suggested intake 2,200." Last update 10-04, next 10-11.
- My week: avg intake 2,425, 7 of 7 days complete, 14-day rate −0.36 kg/week. Protein 158 g vs 157 target. Goal 80 kg ~12–20 weeks away.
- Warnings: only the "macros add up to ~X kcal" one.
- What I think: maintenance ~2,700 so eating 2,400 I'm still in a small deficit — the −0.36 kg/week fits. "On track" feels generous because I've been ~225 kcal over the 2,200 target every day. The numbers didn't change all week (weekly update), which is calmer than my old app.
- Decision: try to actually hit 2,200 (plan 2200). No body fat to log, no scale for it.

## Day 8 (Sun 2026-10-11) — first weekly update after the migration
- From today I use a small script in my folder (doday.mjs) that reads my life log and taps/types through the app the same way I did by hand (+ Weight, Food, Add entry, Day complete).
- Weekly update came in: maintenance dropped 2,720 -> **2,620 ± 280** (Measured, 78%), target 2,200 -> **2,100**. Recommendation no longer "On track": "Your estimated rate (−0.50 to +0.09 kg/week) doesn't include your target of −0.53 kg/week. Eating about 310 kcal/day less than recently would close the gap. Suggested intake 2,100." Avg intake 2,471, 14-day rate −0.21 kg/wk.
- Clear message, I get it: I've been eating too much. Following it -> plan 2100.
- The "2026-10-07: macros add up to ~1680 kcal…" warning is still on the main Nutrition card 4 days later. Feels like nagging about an old day I can't really fix.

## Days 9–14 (scripted batch)
- Weights 88.0, 88.1, 88.4, 87.7, 86.9, 86.6. Intake 2,357 / 1,975 / 1,824 / 1,654 / 2,320 / 2,111. All days complete. No new popups or banners appeared during the batch. The old macro warning is gone from the card now.

## Week 2 (review on Sat 2026-10-17)
- App (still the 10-11 update): maintenance **2,620 ± 280** Measured 78%, target **2,100**, recommendation "rate −0.50 to +0.09 doesn't include target −0.53; eat ~310 kcal/day less; suggested 2,100".
- My week: avg intake **2,096** (7/7 complete) — I hit it. Weight finally dropping: 86.6 today, goal bar 41%. Trend weight 87.5, 14-day rate still says −0.21 (didn't move since Sunday — seems to only refresh weekly too).
- Protein 147 g vs 158 g target — a bit low, but I'm not going to eat more chicken just for this.
- Decision: keep going at ~2,100 (no plan change). Curious what tomorrow's Sunday update says.

## Day 15 (Sun 2026-10-18) — weekly update
- Back to "**On track.** Your estimated rate (−1.05 to +0.28 kg/week) includes your target of −0.52. Suggested 2,100." Maintenance **2,620 ± 300** (was ± 280), Measured **76%** (was 78%). Avg intake 2,034, 14-day rate −0.39 kg/wk.
- Confused: I've given it another full week of perfect data (weighed daily, every day complete) and the range got *wider* (±280 -> ±300, and the weekly-rate range went from −0.50…+0.09 to −1.05…+0.28), and "% from your data" went *down*. The What's-new popup said the range gets narrower as it learns. Maybe because I changed how much I eat? Not explained anywhere I can see without reading the formulas.
- Macro warning back for today's meals (label numbers again).
- Decision: stay at 2,100.

## Days 16–21 (scripted batch)
- Weights 87.0, 87.3, 87.8, 87.3, 86.7, 86.6. Intake 1,643 / 2,025 / 2,188 / 2,467 / 2,109 / 2,263. All complete. Nothing new popped up on opening the app each morning.

## Week 3 (review on Sat 2026-10-24)
- App (10-18 update): maintenance **2,620 ± 300**, Measured 76%, target **2,100**, "On track" (rate −1.05 to +0.28 includes −0.52), suggested 2,100.
- Me: avg 2,099 (7/7 complete). Scale bouncing 86.6–87.8, only ~1 kg under where I started 3 weeks ago. Honestly "On track" at −0.39 kg/wk when the target is −0.52 feels a bit generous, but the range is huge so I guess anything counts.
- The macro warning for 10-18 is still sitting on top of the card six days later.
- Decision: keep 2,100.

## Day 22 (Sun 2026-10-25) — weekly update
- Maintenance **2,610 ± 290**, Measured 76%, target **2,090**, "On track" (rate −0.87 to +0.34 includes −0.52). Avg intake 2,174, 14-day rate −0.26 kg/wk. Target nudged down by 10 kcal — basically the same.
- Mandi + kabsa day, 2,520. Oh well.

## Days 23–28 (scripted batch)
- Weights 87.3, 86.9, 87.0, 86.5, 86.9, 86.4. Intake 1,904 / 2,066 / 2,025 / 2,021 / 2,144 / 2,035. All complete. No new popups/banners on opening.

## Week 4 (review on Sat 2026-10-31)
- App (10-25 update): maintenance **2,610 ± 290**, **Measured** 76%, target **2,090**, "On track" (−0.87 to +0.34 includes −0.52), suggested 2,090.
- Me: avg 2,102 (7/7 complete), 14-day −0.26 kg/wk, trend weight 87.0 (started the 4 weeks at a trend of 87.4). Goal bar 42% → 80 kg. Protein dipped to 130 g vs 157 g target.
- Body composition card has said "Not enough data yet" for 4 weeks — I don't have a body-fat scale, so I guess it'll always say that.
- What I think: I did what it said (≈2,100 for 3 weeks) and I'm only ~0.4 kg (trend) down in a month. "On track" feels too optimistic; I'd have liked it to push me a bit lower. Next week I'd aim for ~2,000 on my own.

## End tasks (Sat 2026-10-31)
- ⇩ -> "Your data": Weigh-ins 73 (45 old + 28 new), Food entries 161 (49 old + 112 new), Complete days 77 (49 old + 28 new). All adds up.
- Full backup (JSON) -> downloads/bodytracker-backup-2026-10-31.json. Opened it: my 177 cm / 32 y / male / light / lose 0.6% profile, goal 80 kg, all 73 weights and 161 food entries. Compared against the backup I made on day 1: every old weight and food entry is still there with the same numbers. Tiny oddity: inside the new backup file "lastBackupAt" still says 2026-10-04 (the file records the backup before this one).
- Daily export, All data, with individual food entries -> downloads/bodytracker-daily_2026-08-05_to_2026-10-31.json: 85 days, per-day weight, calories, macros, complete flag, and each meal with its label. Readable enough. Days where one meal had no carbs/fat just leave carbs/fat out of the day total.
- In 4 weeks the app never reminded me to back up again (last backup was 27 days old when I opened the data screen). Not sure if it's supposed to.

## Final review
The update went smoothly for me: the What's-new popup couldn't be dismissed by accident, it told me straight that my data was safe, and it caught that I'd never set my height and age — the profile step with the "we filled in 175 cm / 25 y automatically" note was genuinely useful. All two months of old weights and daily totals came across and were auto-marked complete. Logging meals separately is nicer than one total. The weekly Sunday update is calm, and the week-2 message ("eat about 310 kcal less") was the clearest thing the app told me; I followed it. What bugged me: the "macros add up to ~X kcal" warning nags on most days and sticks around for days; the ± range got wider instead of narrower after more perfect data; "On track" felt too generous when I'd only lost ~0.4 kg of trend in a month; no "remaining today" number while logging; the Explain-the-math page is formulas I can't read; and the body-composition card says "Not enough data yet" forever without a body-fat scale. Would keep using: yes, probably — it's a proper upgrade over the old version.
agentReply:
# p24 — final reply (32 y/o man, 177 cm, 88 kg, upgrading from the old BodyTracker)

## 1. Usage
- Used the app 28 of 28 days (2026-10-04 → 2026-10-31). 112 meals logged (4 a day), 28/28 days marked complete, 28 weigh-ins (day 1's weigh-in went in through the profile form).
- After the update the app holds 73 weigh-ins, 161 food entries and 77 complete days (45/49/49 old + 28/112/28 new).

## Update-specific findings
- **Popup:** "What's new in BodyTracker" opened first. Tapping the dark area outside it did nothing and the popup stayed open, so you can't skip it by accident (screens/1790454604966.png). The text is long and you have to scroll to reach the buttons "Make a backup" and "Next: confirm your profile". "Make a backup" doesn't save a file itself. It closes the popup and opens a "Your data" panel, where you tap "Full backup (JSON)". When I closed that panel, the profile step still came up, so going to backups first didn't break the flow.
- **Migration:** all my old data survived. The data panel showed 45 weigh-ins and 49 food entries covering 2026-08-05 → 2026-10-03. Old weights appear under Recent entries, and old daily totals open in the Food log by date. I compared my day-1 backup with the final one: every old entry is there with the same values. All 49 old food days were marked "Day complete" automatically, without asking me (fine, because each was a full-day total).
- **Profile step:** a yellow note said "Earlier versions filled in height 175 cm, age 25 and activity 1.45 automatically…". That was exactly my case. The fields were prefilled with 175 / 25 / 86.5 kg (my last old weigh-in) / Male / Lightly active. I changed them to 177 / 32 / 88.1 and answered "Yes" (eating the same for 2+ weeks). The new values were saved and used right away ("Explain the math" shows 177 and 32). Two small things: the note mentions activity 1.45, but it quietly picked Lightly active ×1.375. Changing the weight in the form adds a weigh-in, but the form warns you about that.

## 2. Weekly table
| week | maintenance shown | target | label | recommendation (short) | what I did |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (10-04 update) | 2,720 ± 280 | 2,200 | Measured (78%) | On track, suggested 2,200 | averaged 2,425; plan 2200 |
| 2 (10-11 update) | 2,620 ± 280 | 2,100 | Measured (78%) | Not on track: eat ~310 kcal/day less, suggested 2,100 | plan 2100; averaged 2,096 |
| 3 (10-18 update) | 2,620 ± 300 | 2,100 | Measured (76%) | On track (−1.05 to +0.28 kg/wk), 2,100 | kept 2,100; averaged 2,099 |
| 4 (10-25 update) | 2,610 ± 290 | 2,090 | Measured (76%) | On track (−0.87 to +0.34), 2,090 | kept ~2,100; averaged 2,102 |

## 3. Confusions
- What's-new popup: "Make a backup" opens a panel instead of making the backup.
- Profile step: the note says activity 1.45, but the choices are ×1.375 and ×1.55, and it chose 1.375 without saying so.
- Body tab: tapping the big weight number opens the trend chart, not "add weigh-in" (that is "+ Weight").
- Body tab: it reopens at the old scroll position (halfway down), so at first I thought my weigh-in hadn't saved.
- Food log: once any meal has no macros, the day total shows only kcal, and protein, carbs and fat vanish.
- Food log: there is no "remaining today" figure against the target.
- Nutrition card: the "macros add up to ~X kcal (N% apart)" warning comes up most days and stays on the main card for up to 6 days afterwards.
- Nutrition card: after a week of full, perfect data the range got wider (±280 to ±300, weekly-rate band −0.50…+0.09 to −1.05…+0.28) and "% from your data" dropped 78 to 76. The What's-new popup had said the range narrows as the app learns.
- Nutrition card: it says "On track" at −0.26 to −0.39 kg/wk against a −0.52 target, which feels generous.
- Explain the math: it's pure formulas (Hall/Forbes/MAD). I couldn't follow it.
- Body composition card: it said "Not enough data yet" for all 4 weeks, with no hint that it needs body fat.
- Profile window: Escape doesn't close it (✕ does).

## 4. Possible bugs
- No real bugs found. Everything I logged saved correctly, and the counts match.
- Minor: I made no backup after day 1 and got no backup reminder in 27 days (backup meta shows backupReminderDismissedAt: null). This may be intended.
- Minor: inside bodytracker-backup-2026-10-31.json, meta.lastBackupAt says 2026-10-04, the previous backup's date, even though the screen shows "Last backup: 2026-10-31".
- Files: downloads/bodytracker-backup-2026-10-04.json, downloads/bodytracker-backup-2026-10-31.json, downloads/bodytracker-daily_2026-08-05_to_2026-10-31.json.

## 5. Review
The update was painless. I couldn't close the popup by accident, it told me my data was safe (and it was), and it caught that I'd never set my real height and age. The week-2 "eat ~310 kcal less" message was clear and I followed it. After that, though, "On track" felt too easy on me for a month in which my trend weight dropped only ~0.4 kg. The macro-mismatch warnings and the formula page are noise to me. Would keep using: **yes**.
